page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V, configured with dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 hardware running at 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance carries 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Integrated local storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-speed scratch space directly on the host node. There are no discrete GPUs assigned to this instance, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional single-core processing capabilities, placing stress-ng single-core performance and single-threaded gzip compression within the top tier. The instance also shows strong multi-threaded decompression, PassMark CPU evaluation, and high static web serving throughput reaching 43.7 GB/sec.

Memory throughput and multi-core stress testing operate within median ranges, as seen in uncached memory reads of 107.09 GB/sec and standard multi-core stress scores. The compact 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio represents a cost-efficient resource density for compute-bound operations that do not require deep memory pools, avoiding the overhead of unutilized RAM. Workloads requiring extreme memory footprints will find the 64.0 GB ceiling restrictive, but tasks benefiting from rapid local NVMe IOPS and high clock speeds run effectively.
The D32alds_v7 is technically well matched for batch compression pipelines, continuous integration runners, high-throughput static web servers, and local NVMe-dependent processing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor across 16 physical cores. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions, VAES cryptography, and a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage without GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and compression tasks, paired with strong PassMark CPU results and 43.7 GB/sec static web throughput. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides resource density for compute-driven tasks that do not demand extensive memory allocations. The instance fits high-rate web serving, CI/CD pipelines, compression routines, and local scratch disk workflows.
